verses.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless, like a breath of wind."
What do people gain from all the hard work they do under the sun?
One generation goes, and another generation comes, but the earth stays forever.
The sun rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries back to the place where it rises.
The wind blows to the south, and turns around to the north. It keeps turning around as it goes, and the wind comes back again to its paths.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is never full. The rivers go back to the place they flow from, and they flow again.
Everything is more tiring than words can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, and the ear is never filled with hearing.
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done. There is nothing new under the sun.
Is there anything people can point to and say, "Look, this is new"? It was already here long ago, in the ages before us.
No one remembers the people who came before, and the people still to come will not be remembered by those who come after them.
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I set my heart to search out and explore with wisdom everything that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to people to keep them busy.
I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and look, everything is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.
I said to myself, "Look, I have gained great wisdom, more than anyone who ruled Jerusalem before me. Yes, my heart has learned a great deal of wisdom and knowledge."
I set my heart to understand wisdom, and also madness and foolishness. I learned that this too was like chasing the wind.
For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and the more knowledge you gain, the more grief you have.
